haiku-low.q1: A PR builds the image and runs make test-unit, never deploys. A merge to main starts a run that can deploy.
haiku-low.q2: Both deploy registry.internal/shop-api:SHA, the image built once after merge. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
haiku-low.q3: Integration failure: one automatic retry for a known flaky test; if it fails again, the run fails. Unit failure: no retry, the other test job is cancelled and the run fails.
haiku-low.q4: Staging runs the previous_tag image via rollback, with the migrated schema kept. The image is found from /deploy/staging/previous_tag in SSM.
haiku-low.q5: Only members of release-approvers, never the commit's author. If no approval within 72 hours, the run expires and nothing goes to production.
haiku-low.q6: In SSM Parameter Store: /deploy/<env>/current_tag and previous_tag, written by deploy.sh only after a successful staging or production rollout.
haiku-low.q7: canary-off runs and the run fails. Stable deployment and SSM tags are unchanged, but the production schema stays migrated ahead of the stable image.
haiku-low.q8: It ends quietly as superseded: no deploy, no alert, locks released. It stops because current_tag equals or is a descendant of its SHA.
haiku-low.q9: Outside the window it waits holding no lock. While another production deploy runs, it queues for the lock, then rechecks the window and waits again if past 15:00.
haiku-low.q10: The canary's 5xx ratio over the last minute, from Prometheus, sampled every 30s for 15 min. Failure: any sample above 1%, or two no-data samples in a row after minute 2.
haiku-low.q11: NOT STATED. The document says only that CI manual approval records approver and time, with a 72-hour deadline; notification and decision information are not stated.
haiku-low.q12: NOT STATED as an automatic return. A failed deploy script triggers no rollback; a person inspects the cluster, since rollback would pick the wrong tag before SSM is written.

sonnet.q1: A pull request builds the image and runs unit tests (make test-unit); it never deploys and pushes nothing. A merge to main starts a run that can deploy.
sonnet.q2: Both deploy the one image registry.internal/shop-api:SHA (SHA = full commit hash of the merge), built once and pushed. Nothing is rebuilt after the tests.
sonnet.q3: Integration test failure: it is retried automatically once (known flaky test); if it fails again, the unit job is cancelled and the failure is announced in #deploys. Unit test failure: no retry; the integration job is cancelled and the failure is announced in #deploys. The run ends failed.
sonnet.q4: Staging rolls back with deploy.sh rollback staging, which sets the image back to previous_tag (read from SSM) and writes current_tag = previous_tag. Staging ends on the previous image; the schema stays as migrated. Failure is announced in #deploys.
sonnet.q5: Only members of the release-approvers group, and not the author of the merged commit (that approval is void). If nobody approves within 72 hours of the smoke test passing, expiry is announced in #deploys, nothing goes to production, staging keeps this SHA, and the run ends as expired.
sonnet.q6: In AWS SSM Parameter Store, kept by deploy.sh: /deploy/<env>/current_tag and /deploy/<env>/previous_tag. They are written only after the rollout succeeds (previous_tag = old current, current_tag = SHA). The pipeline only reads them. The canary is never recorded.
sonnet.q7: The stable deployment is untouched and still runs the old image. SSM tags are unchanged because canary writes nothing to SSM. The production database schema stays migrated forward, since migrations run at canary start and nothing undoes them. deploy.sh canary-off scales the canary to 0 and the failure is announced in #deploys. There is no automatic production rollback.
sonnet.q8: The older run is superseded. After it takes the production lock it reads /deploy/production/current_tag. If its SHA equals that tag or is an ancestor of it, the run ends quietly with no deploy and no post. NOT STATED: what exactly the document says about a newer run only reaching staging, since the check reads the production tag, not staging; the staging check happens at the staging lock.
sonnet.q9: Outside the window (Mon-Thu 09:00-15:00 UTC) it waits for the next window start, holding no lock. If another production deploy holds production-deploy, it queues behind that lock. After getting the lock it rechecks the window; if the window has closed, it releases the lock and waits for the next window. It then does the superseded check before starting the canary.
sonnet.q10: The canary's 5xx ratio over the last 1 minute, queried from Prometheus (query in environments.md), sampled every 30 s for 15 min (30 samples). It fails on any sample above 1%, or on 2 consecutive no-data samples after minute 2 (no-data is ignored in the first 2 minutes). On failure it runs canary-off and announces the failure.
sonnet.q11: NOT STATED. The document says only that a manual approval job exists, restricted to release-approvers, and that CI records who approved and when. It does not say how approvers are notified or what information they see.
sonnet.q12: It is not rolled back. If deploy.sh staging or production fails partway, no rollback is run, because the SSM tags are written only after rollout succeeds, so current_tag would still name the old version and rollback would restore previous_tag, one version too far back. Instead the #deploys post says the cluster may be partway through a rollout while SSM shows the old tag, a person inspects the cluster, and the next successful deploy to that environment corrects SSM.
